title: Lesson 30 - Canvas and Script View: Two Surfaces, One Agent
description: Explain the components and benefits of hybrid reasoning, including how Agent Script functions in Canvas and Script View.

questions.question: An admin configures conditional action availability and quick if-then transitions using blocks and shortcuts. Which surface are they using?
options: Canvas view, using the pattern and resource shortcuts
questions.explanation: Canvas view is the low-code surface where blocks, action filters, and the pattern and resource shortcuts configure transitions and conditional availability without touching syntax.

questions.question: Which artifact does Canvas view ultimately produce?
options: Agent Script, the same single source Script view edits, which compiles to the Agent Graph
questions.explanation: Canvas produces Agent Script, the one source both views edit, and that script compiles to the Agent Graph the runtime executes, so Canvas never produces a Flow or a document.

questions.question: A team wants complex action chaining where a sequence of actions runs in a guaranteed order, plus fine-grained conditional branching. Which surface fits best?
options: Canvas view with the pattern shortcut
Script view, where complex expressions and action chaining belong
A price book entry per action
questions.explanation: Complex expressions, action chaining in a guaranteed order, and fine-grained branching belong in Script view, while Canvas is stronger for standard blocks and quick transitions.
